answer: Scarce-Resource Registration. Each identity must complete a randomly assigned physical task at a verified site, such as a copper-wire continuity check at a registered depot. A regional coordinator near an oasis validates completion and signs the credential. Because task slots per site are limited by throughput, an attacker must recruit many real accomplices or travel widely; duplicating identities costs repeated verified labor and travel, not just money. Credentials expire unless renewed at a willow-marked station.
